name: Google Ads
summary: Spend, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Google Ads accounts.
description: Signs in with Google and reads every Google Ads account the sign-in can see, including accounts under a manager account. Google also asks for a developer token: create one in your own Google Ads manager account (Admin, API Center) and add it after signing in. Read-only: nothing changes in your accounts.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

name: LinkedIn Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and conversions per campaign from your LinkedIn ad accounts.
description: Signs in with LinkedIn and reads every ad account the member can see, with read-only access. Conversions are LinkedIn's website conversions as LinkedIn counts them.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

name: Meta Ads
summary: Spend, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Facebook and Instagram ad accounts.
description: Reads every ad account a token can see, with read-only access. The simplest way: in your Meta Business Settings, Users, System users, create a system user, give it the ad accounts, and generate a token with the ads_read permission. Conversions are Meta's standard events (purchases, leads, registrations, trials, subscriptions).
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

name: Microsoft Advertising
summary: Spend, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Microsoft Advertising (Bing) accounts.
description: Signs in with Microsoft and reads every Microsoft Advertising account the sign-in can see. Microsoft also asks for a developer token: get your own from the Microsoft Advertising developer portal (Account, Request token) and add it after signing in. Read-only.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

name: Reddit Ads
summary: Spend, impressions and clicks per campaign from your Reddit ad accounts.
description: Signs in with Reddit and reads every ad account of every business the account belongs to, with read-only access. Separate from organic Reddit, which posts and listens from your brand's own account.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

name: X Ads
summary: Spend, impressions and clicks per campaign from your X ad accounts.
description: Uses your own X developer app, once X has approved it for the Ads API (apply in the developer portal; approval can take a few weeks). Paste the app's API key and secret and the access token and secret of the account that runs your ads. Read-only.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

name: Amplitude
summary: Active users, page views, top pages and event counts from Amplitude.
description: Reads one project with its API key and secret key. Traffic uses active users and the [Amplitude] Page Viewed event from the browser SDK.

name: Bing Webmaster Tools
summary: Clicks, impressions and the search queries people used on Bing before visiting your site.
description: Reads every verified site in your Bing Webmaster Tools account. Bing keeps about six months of search data.

name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
summary: Page views, visits, top pages and referrers from Cloudflare's free Web Analytics.
description: Reads every Web Analytics site on one Cloudflare account. Cloudflare counts visits and page views but not unique visitors.

name: Fathom Analytics
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers and event conversions from Fathom.
description: Reads every site on the account with an API key. Events count as conversions.

name: Google Analytics
summary: Visitors, top pages, traffic sources and key events from Google Analytics 4.
description: Signs in with Google (or uses a service account key) and reads any GA4 property the account can see, with read-only access. Pick the property once, or name it on each call. Conversions are GA4 key events. The same sign-in also connects Search Console.

name: Google Search Console
summary: What people search on Google before they click through to your site, and how you rank.
description: Signs in with Google (or uses a service account key) and reads every Search Console property the account can see, with read-only access. Domain properties show as sc-domain:example.com. The same sign-in also connects Google Analytics.

name: Matomo
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers, events and goal conversions from Matomo, cloud or self-hosted.
description: Reads every site the token can view. The token is sent in the request body, never the address.

name: Microsoft Clarity
summary: Sessions, visitors and frustration signals (rage and dead clicks) from Clarity, for the last three days.
description: Clarity's export API only covers the last one to three days and allows ten calls a day per project, so Outflare keeps each answer for six hours. Use it for a recent snapshot, not history.

name: Mixpanel
summary: Page views, pages, referrers and event counts from Mixpanel.
description: Uses a service account. Traffic comes from Mixpanel's page view event ($mp_web_page_view unless you name another). Mixpanel allows about 60 report queries an hour, so Outflare keeps each answer for an hour.

name: Plausible
summary: Visitors, pages, sources and goal conversions from Plausible, cloud or self-hosted.
description: Reads one site with a Stats API key. Goals count as conversions.

name: PostHog
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers and custom events from PostHog. Sign in with PostHog Cloud, US or EU, or use a personal API key.
description: Signs in with PostHog and reads the projects you allow, with read-only access to queries. A personal API key works too, and is the way for self-hosted PostHog. Visitors are distinct people with a $pageview; sources are the referring domain.

name: Simple Analytics
summary: Visitors, pages and referrers from Simple Analytics.
description: Reads one website. Public dashboards need only the domain; private ones need an API key and your user id.

name: Umami
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers and events from Umami, cloud or self-hosted.
description: Umami Cloud: paste an API key. Self-hosted: give the address and a user that can view the websites; Outflare signs in for each report.

name: Vercel Web Analytics
summary: Page views, visitors, top pages, referrers and custom events from Vercel Web Analytics.
description: Reads every project on one Vercel account or team. Only production traffic counts, as on Vercel's own dashboard. Projects need Web Analytics turned on.
pricing: Free on Hobby, more events on Pro

name: Cal.com
summary: Count meetings leads book through your Cal.com links.
description: Reads your Cal.com bookings and their attendees. Nothing is changed in Cal.com.

name: Calendly
summary: Count meetings leads book through your Calendly links.
description: Reads scheduled events for your Calendly organization and their invitees. Nothing is changed in Calendly.

name: Google Calendar
summary: Count meetings booked with leads, from any Google Workspace or Gmail calendar.
description: Reads events from one calendar (the primary one unless calendar_id is set) and keeps only those with a lead or a lead's colleague among the guests. Nothing is written to the calendar.

name: Outlook Calendar
summary: Count meetings booked with leads, from a Microsoft 365 or Outlook.com calendar.
description: Reads the signed-in person's calendar and keeps only meetings with a lead or a lead's colleague among the attendees. Nothing is written to the calendar.

name: GitHub
summary: Know when your website's repository ships, so fixes are re-checked and experiments start on the real deploy.
description: Reads your repositories' production deployments, or pushes to the default branch when a repository records no deployments. Outflare never pushes code, opens pull requests or changes settings through it.
pricing: Works on every GitHub plan, including free

name: Vercel
summary: Know when your website's Vercel project goes live, so fixes are re-checked and experiments start on the real deploy.
description: Reads your projects' production deployments and the domains they serve. Outflare never deploys, promotes, rolls back or changes settings through it.
pricing: Works on every Vercel plan, including Hobby

name: Attio
summary: Bring your Attio CRM over: see every object, field and list it holds, then import it once.
description: Reads your Attio workspace's objects (People, Companies, Deals and custom ones), their fields, lists and pipelines, and counts records, entries, notes and tasks, so you can see what moving over brings before anything is copied. Read-only: Outflare never changes anything in Attio.
pricing: Works on every Attio plan, including Free

name: HubSpot
summary: Count meetings and deals from outreach, and log booked meetings on the contact.
description: Reads deals (stage, amount, close date) and meetings, and ties each to the lead and campaign that started it. Optionally writes meetings booked from outreach onto the HubSpot contact (off by default, since HubSpot may already log them from its own calendar sync). Deals are never changed.
pricing: Works on every HubSpot plan, including free

name: Apollo
summary: Search Apollo's people database and reveal work emails with your Apollo credits.
description: Build lists from Apollo searches by title, seniority, company size, industry and location. Searching is free; revealing an email uses one Apollo credit per person found. Mailboxes also connected in Apollo are flagged on the Mailboxes page, since Apollo may send from them too.
pricing: Free search; one credit per revealed email

name: Findymail
summary: Find verified work emails from a name and company domain.
description: Fills in verified work emails for people found elsewhere. Charges only when it finds one.

name: LeadMagic
summary: Find work emails from a name and company domain.
description: Fills in work emails for people found elsewhere. Charges only when it finds a valid address.

name: MoltSets
summary: Search B2B people and find valid work emails with your own MoltSets plan.
description: Build lists from MoltSets people searches by title, seniority, industry, company size, country, company domain and keywords, and find work emails from a LinkedIn URL, an email, or a name with a company domain. Each email carries MoltSets' send-safety grade.
pricing: Flat monthly plans with fair-use limits; a free tier of 1,000 tokens

name: People Data Labs
summary: Search and enrich people from People Data Labs with your own credits.
description: Build lists from People Data Labs searches by title, seniority, industry, company size and location, and fill in missing fields on leads you already have.

name: Prospeo
summary: Find verified work emails from a name and company, or a LinkedIn URL.
description: Fills in work emails for people found elsewhere. Only verified addresses are returned, and you are charged only when one is found.

name: Cloudflare
summary: Add the DNS records Outflare needs (site verification, sending and tracking domains) in one click.
description: Outflare only adds records, each with the comment "Added by Outflare": it never changes or deletes one. With an API token, use the "Edit zone DNS" template, limited to the zones you want Outflare to write to.

name: Amazon SES
summary: Send transactional and lifecycle email from your own AWS account, at about $0.10 per 1,000 emails.
description: Outflare sends through your Amazon SES account with an IAM access key. It registers your domain with Easy DKIM and a custom MAIL FROM subdomain, and sets up a configuration set and an SNS topic so deliveries, bounces and complaints come back automatically. SES is for mail people asked for: never cold email.
pricing: Pay AWS directly: about $0.10 per 1,000 emails

name: Postmark
summary: Send transactional email through Postmark, known for fast, reliable delivery of receipts and password resets.
description: Outflare sends through one of your Postmark servers and registers a webhook on it, so deliveries, bounces and spam complaints come back automatically. Add the account token too and Outflare also adds your sending domain with its DKIM and return-path records.
pricing: Pay Postmark directly; 100 test emails a month free

name: Resend
summary: Send transactional and lifecycle email through Resend, the developer-first email API.
description: Outflare sends through your Resend account, adds your sending domain with its DKIM, SPF and MX records, and registers a signed webhook so deliveries, bounces and complaints come back automatically.
pricing: Pay Resend directly; 3,000 emails a month free

name: Bouncer
summary: EU-hosted email verification with toxicity checks.
description: Verifies each address and reports catch-all, disposable and role accounts, with a 0–100 score.

name: DeBounce
summary: Email verification that marks addresses safe to send, risky or invalid.
description: Verifies each address and flags spam traps, disposable, catch-all and role addresses.

name: Emailable
summary: Email verification with a quality score for every address.
description: Verifies each address and returns a state, a reason and a 0–100 score.

name: Hunter
summary: Find and verify work emails with Hunter.
description: Verifies each address with SMTP checks and a confidence score.
pricing: Monthly plans with search and verification credits

name: MillionVerifier
summary: Low-cost email verification popular with cold email teams.
description: Verifies each address and marks catch-all, disposable and role addresses.

name: NeverBounce
summary: Real-time email verification with a deliverability guarantee.
description: Verifies each address and flags disposable and catch-all domains.

name: Reoon Email Verifier
summary: Low-cost verification with a power mode that checks the mailbox over SMTP.
description: Verifies each address in power mode and flags catch-all, disposable, role and full mailboxes.
pricing: Pay per credit; unknown results are refunded

name: ZeroBounce
summary: Email validation with spam-trap, abuse and catch-all detection.
description: Checks each address before it is emailed and flags spam traps, known complainers and catch-all domains.

name: Cheap Inboxes
summary: Import your Google and Microsoft mailboxes from Cheap Inboxes and keep them in sync.
description: Connect your Cheap Inboxes account with an API key. Outflare lists every mailbox, imports the ones you pick (or all of them, automatically) with their passwords, checks SMTP, IMAP and DNS, and picks up new and cancelled mailboxes on its own. Google mailboxes get an app password from Cheap Inboxes, since Google refuses plain passwords.

name: Claude
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Claude API key. Anthropic's Claude models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the project brief and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Claude's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Claude account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Claude

name: Gemini
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Gemini API key. Google's Gemini models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the project brief and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Gemini's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Gemini account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Gemini

name: Mistral
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Mistral API key. Mistral's models, hosted in the EU.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the project brief and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Mistral's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Mistral account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Mistral

name: OpenAI
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own OpenAI API key. OpenAI's GPT models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the project brief and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to OpenAI's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your OpenAI account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by OpenAI

name: OpenRouter
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own OpenRouter API key. Hundreds of models from many vendors (OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, Perplexity...) with one key; OpenRouter reports what each call cost.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the project brief and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to OpenRouter's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your OpenRouter account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by OpenRouter

name: Stripe
summary: See who pays you: customers, subscriptions, payments and refunds on each person's record.
description: Reads your Stripe customers, subscriptions, payments and refunds, every few minutes. Each customer becomes a person with their plan, monthly revenue, lifetime revenue and billing status, and each payment is an event on their timeline, so the CRM, lifecycle email, missions and partners all use the same numbers. Read-only: Outflare never charges, refunds or changes anything in Stripe.
pricing: Free: Stripe does not charge for API calls

name: Ahrefs
summary: Domain Rating, backlinks, organic keywords, competitors and Site Audit health for your domains.
description: Needs an Ahrefs plan with API access and an API key. Reads Site Explorer for any domain and Site Audit for projects your account already crawls. Calls spend Ahrefs API units; Outflare records an estimate of each call in Outcomes and stops at the connection's monthly budget.
pricing: API units from your Ahrefs plan

name: DataForSEO
summary: Keyword rankings, rank tracking, estimated search traffic, competitors and backlinks for any domain, paid per call.
description: Uses DataForSEO Labs for rankings, traffic and competitors, the SERP API to track where your pages rank on Google, and the Backlinks API for links (a separate DataForSEO subscription; without it the overview skips links). Every call's cost comes back from DataForSEO and is recorded in Outcomes; a monthly budget on the connection stops calls before they go over.
pricing: Pay per call, about $0.01 to $0.05 a report

name: Geonode
summary: Searches the web, finds your brands' social links, reads public X follower counts, and reads your own site's pages when a firewall blocks OutflareBot.
description: Runs web searches for finding companies and pages, through Geonode's Search API. Reads each brand's homepage to suggest its social profiles and app store listings, and the public X profile in each brand's links once a day for its follower count. For sites you have proved you own, and only for pages robots.txt allows: when a page answers with a firewall block or a challenge, OutflareBot reads it through Geonode's Scraper API instead. Searches and pages cost Geonode tokens on your account.
pricing: Tokens per search and per page, on your Geonode plan

name: EmailBison
summary: Let Outflare decide which sender emails each EmailBison campaign uses.
description: Outflare reads your sender emails and campaigns every few minutes, adds and removes sender emails on campaigns as mailbox allocation decides, and accepts changes you make in EmailBison as manual ones. Replies your campaigns get come into the Outflare inbox, labelled, and you can answer them there.

name: Instantly
summary: Switching from Instantly? Import campaigns, leads and sending accounts in one go.
description: Reads your Instantly campaigns (with every step and variant), their leads and where each lead got to, and your sending accounts. Importing only reads. Once connected, mailbox allocation also adds and removes sending accounts on Instantly campaigns, and accepts changes you make in Instantly as manual ones.
pricing: Included in Instantly's Hypergrowth plan and above

name: Smartlead
summary: Switching from Smartlead? Import campaigns, leads and email accounts in one go.
description: Reads your Smartlead campaigns (with every step and variant), their leads and where each lead got to, and your email accounts. Importing only reads. Once connected, mailbox allocation also adds and removes email accounts on Smartlead campaigns, and accepts changes you make in Smartlead as manual ones.

name: LinkedIn
summary: Track followers and posts of your company pages and profile, and post from them.
description: Sign in with your own LinkedIn account: Outflare reaches your profile and every company page you administer. LinkedIn's API is free; on a self-hosted server, register a LinkedIn app with the Community Management API and set CONNECTOR_LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID and CONNECTOR_LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET.

name: Reddit
summary: Find threads where your brand can help, and post approved replies from your brand's own account.
description: Uses your own Reddit app, so searches and posts run on your Reddit API access. Make a web app at reddit.com/prefs/apps with this server's redirect URI, paste its client id and secret, then sign in with the brand's Reddit account to post replies a person approved. Every reply says who wrote it.
pricing: Reddit's Data API terms apply to your app

name: X
summary: Track your brand's X followers and posts, and post from its own account.
description: Uses your own X developer app, so X bills your account for API use (pay per use). Make an app in the X developer console with OAuth 2.0 turned on (type: web app) and this server's redirect URI, paste its OAuth 2.0 client id and secret, then sign in with the brand's X account.
pricing: X bills your developer account per use

name: Google Tag Manager
summary: Add Outflare's website script to your site in one click, through your own Tag Manager container.
description: Outflare adds one Custom HTML tag named "Outflare" that fires on all pages, in a Tag Manager workspace of its own, so nobody else's unpublished changes go live with it. It never edits or removes your other tags.

name: Hotjar
summary: Hotjar's API covers surveys and user lookups, not traffic, so there is nothing to report yet.

name: Segment
summary: Segment forwards events but does not count visits. Planned as a source of events, not a report.

name: Chili Piper
summary: Meetings booked through Chili Piper routers.

name: SavvyCal
summary: Meetings booked through SavvyCal links.

name: Zoom Scheduler
summary: Meetings booked through Zoom Scheduler.

name: Pipedrive
summary: Create deals in Pipedrive from interested replies.

name: Salesforce
summary: Sync replies, interested leads and meetings to Salesforce.

name: BetterContact
summary: Waterfall email and phone finding.

name: Clay
summary: Send enriched rows from a Clay table straight into a list.

name: Cognism
summary: Search Cognism's European-strong contact data.

name: ContactOut
summary: Emails and phones from LinkedIn profiles.

name: Dropcontact
summary: GDPR-friendly email finding and enrichment.

name: FullEnrich
summary: Waterfall email and phone finding across many sources.

name: Icypeas
summary: Low-cost email finding and verification.

name: Lusha
summary: Find emails and phone numbers with your Lusha credits.

name: RocketReach
summary: Search people and reveal emails and phones.

name: Wiza
summary: Emails and phones for LinkedIn and Sales Navigator lists.

name: ZoomInfo
summary: Search ZoomInfo contacts and companies with your own licence.

name: Amazon Route 53
summary: Set SPF, DKIM, DMARC and tracking records automatically.

name: GoDaddy
summary: Set SPF, DKIM, DMARC and tracking records automatically.

name: Namecheap
summary: Set SPF, DKIM, DMARC and tracking records automatically.

name: Mailgun
summary: Send transactional and lifecycle email through Mailgun.

name: SendGrid
summary: Send transactional and lifecycle email through Twilio SendGrid.

name: BounceBan
summary: Verifies catch-all addresses other tools mark unknown.

name: BriteVerify
summary: Email verification from Validity.

name: Cheap Verifier
summary: Low-cost verification from the Cheap Inboxes team.

name: Clearout
summary: Real-time and bulk email verification.

name: Kickbox
summary: Email verification with a Sendex quality score.

name: Scrubby
summary: Catch-all and unknown address validation.

name: Infraforge
summary: Unconfirmed: no public API checked yet. Upload its mailboxes by SMTP and IMAP; they are watched as a sending server.

name: Mailreef
summary: Unconfirmed: no public API checked yet. Upload its mailboxes by SMTP and IMAP; they are watched as a sending server.

name: PlusVibe
summary: Move campaigns, leads and mailboxes over from PlusVibe.

name: Common Room
summary: Community, product and website signals in one place.

name: Crunchbase
summary: Funding rounds and acquisitions as reasons to reach out.

name: PredictLeads
summary: Hiring, news and technology changes at target companies.

name: RB2B
summary: People visiting your website, by name.

name: TheirStack
summary: Companies hiring for roles that signal a need, and the tech they use.

name: Trigify
summary: LinkedIn engagement and job-change signals.

name: UserGems
summary: Past customers and champions who changed jobs.
